_authority: This signed functional specification is the governing reference for the NextPower supplier conversion. Rules here are seeded as client-scoped learnings so they are applied BEFORE deterministic control constants and before AI, and they override any conflicting hardcoded default.

rules.condition: Sandeep 28-Jul: 'It should be corporation... there is one column in the extract, IS INDIVIDUAL. If there is a value in that, only in that case this value will change' -> Individual. Only these two values are ever valid: 'the business will not be value, only corporation or individual will be the values.' A flat CORPORATION constant loaded every individual supplier as a corporation.
rules.status: IMPLEMENTED as CASE_WHEN (engine already supports notblank). ANSWERED by the analyst 30-Jul: the instance expects the DISPLAY value — 'Corporation should not be all caps as well, C caps, rest small'. Values are now Corporation / Individual. Both are registered as protected values so no cleansing family re-cases them. Source column 'Is Individual' still to confirm.
rules.note: INDIVIDUAL only when the source SAYS so. 'Is Individual' is the authority: Yes on 437 of 7,495 rows, No on 6,985, blank on 73. Entity Type is a FALLBACK for rows where Is Individual is silent, and it is explicitly ranked below an outright 'No' -- checked against the data, all 19 rows where the two disagree have Is Individual=No and Entity Type=Individual, and 17 of them are plainly companies (Air Liquide Brasil LTDA, RYNDACK COMERCIO E IMPORTACAO LTDA, EDIFFICA ENGENHARIA E PROJETOS LTDA). Letting Entity Type win flipped those 17 to INDIVIDUAL and could never fill a genuine gap, because this extract has ZERO rows with a blank Is Individual and a populated Entity Type. Earlier the branch read notblank, which made 7,422 of 7,495 suppliers INDIVIDUAL because 'No' is not blank.

Oracle expects the 2-character ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Resolved by lookup (United States->US, Italy->IT), never truncation. Already-valid 2-char codes pass through; an unrecognised country is left unchanged so it surfaces in review rather than becoming a wrong code.
rules.status: IMPLEMENTED - engine rule COUNTRY_ISO2 added, reusing the curated COUNTRY_TO_ISO table
rules.decision_needed: ANALYST SAID "United Kingdom is UK" BUT ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for the UK is GB, and Oracle Fusion TERRITORY_CODE uses ISO. The rule currently returns GB (and also maps a literal "UK" input to GB). If the target instance genuinely expects UK, say so and the table needs an override - otherwise GB is correct and UK would be rejected on load.
